Those who prove their dedication and leadership are lifted up as examples to the younger Solars and to the Cult as a whole, are expected to teach and to lead, and receive a greater portion of the cultists' prayers. As the prophesied Illuminated Ones the Solars receive the greatest consideration within the Cult, and all Illuminated Solars begin with Illumination • for free. Other Exalted serve the Cult and may purchase Illumination, but do not reach the same heights: Dragon-Blooded may not exceed •••, Lunars may reach ••••, Sidereals do not normally take it at all (using Connections (The Cult of the Illuminated) instead), and an Abyssal may take it only with the Storyteller's approval.
ladder: The Exalt has no rank or trust within the Cult. Either he is an outsider, or he is considered a lesser, dedicated servant of the Illuminated, no better than the rank-and-file members of the Cult.

Initiate. The Exalt has achieved the trust and dedication of the Cult, and its resources are at his disposal. Despite this he is still considered unproven, expected to learn at the feet of his instructors; while cultists are required to obey his word, he is expected to listen to the advice of wiser cultists, such as his guide. This is the rank of a Solar training in the camps, and all Illuminated Solars begin here.

Adept. The Exalt has proven himself to the Cult and now acts as an independent agent. He is free to come and go as he pleases, and can expect mortals to listen to his commands as well as tend to his needs. Adepts primarily serve as the agents of the Cult, leaving the camps to perform tasks on their behalf. This is the rank of those Solars who have graduated from their training.

Illuminated. The Exalt has experience in serving the Cult and is considered a leader. Adepts look to him for leadership, and he often leads Cult missions and endeavors. Illuminated Exalts also serve as instructors of less capable Solars, and all the instructors of the camps stand at this rank. They receive a portion of the Cult's worship and, every dawn — the hour of worship for mortals — regain a free point of Willpower.

Saint. The Exalt has proven himself beyond the rest of the Solars and is a hero among the Cult. His name is spoken amongst cultists and he is held up as an example to other Solars. Saints are living embodiments of the Illuminated Ones and serve as the high priests of the Cult, making appearances at gatherings and performing miracles for the believers. In addition to gaining a point of Willpower at every dawn, their hourly Essence regeneration rate is increased by 2.

Prophet. The Exalt leads and guides the whole of the Cult with his words. Training camps are ostensibly headed by prophets, as is the Cult itself. These Solars are the voice of the Cult, speaking for Heaven above, and their word is divine mandate to the cultists below them — though they remain spokesmen for a Heaven run by the Sidereals. In addition to their daily point of Willpower, their hourly Essence regeneration rate is increased by 3.

name: Tiger Warriors
description: Fanatical soldiers willing to fight and die for the Illuminated Ones. In addition to the Solars, the Cult trains elite cadres of mortal soldiers whose dedication to the cause is complete; the greatest are trained by the Solars themselves, their skills augmented by the Charm Tiger-Warrior Training Technique. Lacking the resources of the Realm or the Deathlords, the Gold Faction cannot field nearly as many soldiers, and tiger warriors are a valuable resource not to be thrown away frivolously — yet each looks forward to the day he can become a martyr, assured a place in Heaven beside his beloved Solar. Unlike the faceless legionnaires of the Realm, these warriors each know their leader personally and adore him. Tiger warriors are always considered elite extras.
ladder: Your Solar works alone. Perhaps his training didn't involve leadership, or perhaps the tasks the Cult puts him to would only be hampered by the presence of others. For whatever reason, the Cult has chosen not to bestow your Solar with mortal servants.
A dedicated guard. Your Solar is attended by a personal bodyguard consisting of no more than five tiger warriors and one heroic mortal that sees to his protection and needs.
A crack unit. The Solar has command of a sizable force of tiger warriors, no more than 15, that can act independently of the Solar if necessary. These warriors are led by up to two heroic mortals.

A personal strike force. Up to 25 tiger warriors serve the Solar, acting as an elite strike force ready to carry out his commands. Up to three heroic mortals aid the Solar in the command of this unit or, optionally, a single Dragon-Blood who serves the Solar personally.

A dedicated brigade. The Solar commands a considerable force of tiger warriors, up to 100, enough to intimidate small towns and to fend off a small Wyld Hunt. Alternately, the Solar may lead 50 especially well-trained and -equipped tiger warriors considered superior in quality. In addition, up to four heroic mortals or a single Dragon-Blood attend the Solar.

A small army. Up to 250 tiger warriors of elite quality or 100 tiger warriors of superior quality follow the Solar's every command, a mighty force ready to sacrifice their lives for him. Additionally, up to five heroic mortals serve the Solar. Alternatively, he may be served by an experienced Dragon-Blooded outcaste, or a lone Casteless Lunar acquired and trained before the Silver Pact could reach him, serving as personal attendant, champion and commander of his troops — undeniably great, but dangerously unpredictable.

name: Sorcery
description: A thorough education in the arts of sorcery at a Cult of the Illuminated training camp, granting free spells. Solars stand upon the apex of sorcery, and once taught the basic principles the rest comes easily to them. This Background provides only the knowledge of spells, not the Charms associated with sorcery — to take full advantage of it the character must acquire the appropriate Sorcery Charms through normal Charm selection. The spells gained must be selected from the Cult's approved list: the Gold Faction teaches what is immediately useful and quietly withholds the more controversial spells.
ladder: The character has no special training in sorcery. Far from a deficit, the character has simply chosen to focus on other aspects of her training.
The character has learned the basic principles of the art of sorcery and gains a single spell from the Terrestrial Circle.
The character benefits from extensive training in the occult and gains two spells from the Terrestrial Circle.
The character has mastered the fundamentals of sorcery and gains three spells from the Terrestrial Circle.
The character has extensively studied sorcery, expanding upon the principles taught to her at her training camp, and gains four spells from either the Terrestrial or the Celestial Circles.

The character's knowledge and understanding of sorcery is almost unparalleled. Characters this dedicated to sorcery are destined to shake the world and begin play with five spells from the Terrestrial or the Celestial Circles.

name: Artifact
description: As lords of the Realm, the Dragon-Blooded have inherited a sizable portion of the remains of the First Age's infrastructure, as well as almost the entirety of its arsenal of jade artifacts and wonders. The result is that Dragon-Blooded characters have a much easier time acquiring artifacts than the fallen Anathema, or anyone else for that matter. The Artifact Background grants Dragon-Blooded twice the number of dots' worth of artifacts as normal.
ladder: A single level 1 artifact of the Storyteller's choice.
A pair of level 1 artifacts.
A level 2 artifact, and a pair of level 1 artifacts.
A level 3 artifact, and three dots worth of level 1 and 2 artifacts (either a level 2 artifact and a level 1 artifact, or three level 1 artifacts).
A level 4 artifact, and four dots worth of level 1 through 3 artifacts (a level 3 artifact and a level 1 artifact, a pair of level 2 artifacts, etc.).

A level 5 artifact, and five dots worth of level 1 through 4 artifacts (a level 4 artifact and a level 1 artifact, a level 3 artifact and a level 2 artifact, a pair of level 2 artifacts and a level 1 artifact, etc.). At the Storyteller's discretion, the character may also have access to the Realm's arsenal of First Age war machines — not that this means he'll actually own one, but he may be able to get permission to use one.

name: Manse
description: In contrast to the chaotic and savage Threshold, the Realm is a place of relative order and stability, and imperial forces have managed to locate and claim all known Manses located on the Blessed Isle. Because various Great Houses or the Immaculate Order already hold these Manses, it is exceedingly difficult for a Dragon-Blooded character to claim one as her own personal property. Most households and estates are built around Manses, and being able to purchase the rights to one is essential in starting a household or line. Rather than representing a single Manse the character has claim on, the Manse rating of a Dragon-Blooded character indicates generally how many Manses she has been attuned to. Characters who carry the Hearthstone from a Manse probably don't actually own it, instead holding it on extended loan; in case of family emergency the stone may be recalled, especially a powerful one. Level 1 and 2 Manses are very common in the Realm and are used as weekend and vacation manors, hunting lodges and strongholds to defend small estates.
ladder: The character is not welcome in any of the Realm's Manses. Why?
The character is allowed to enter and has been attuned to several level 1 and 2 Manses. She may have one Hearthstone of level 1 or 2.
The character is allowed to enter and has been attuned to several weak Manses. She has a couple of level 1 or 2 Hearthstones (no more than three levels, total).

The character is allowed to enter and has been attuned to some fairly powerful Manses. She has a level 3 Hearthstone and several level 1 and 2 stones (no more than six levels, total, including the large stone).

The character is allowed to enter and has been attuned to some very powerful Manses, probably among the best her house possesses. She has a level 4 Hearthstone and several of level 1 or 2 and possibly even one of level 3 (no more than eight levels, total, including the large stone).

The character is allowed to enter and attune herself to the Realm's most powerful Manses, and has even been entrusted with the Hearthstone of one of these cathedrals of the Exalted. She has a level 5 Hearthstone and several others of level 1-3 (no more than ten levels, total, including the large stone).

name: Artifact
description: The Deathlords rule vast kingdoms within the Underworld, and their favored servants are able to take full advantage of the resources at their liege's command — deathknights have a much easier time acquiring artifacts than most other Exalted. All a deathknight's artifacts are forged from soulsteel unless the Storyteller gives specific permission otherwise, and are frequently disturbing blends of grotesque beauty and fascinating horror: the faces of the dead are reflected in their surfaces, and the screams and moans of the dead issue forth softly now and then. Jade, usually taken from grave goods, is the second most common Magical Material. Abyssal characters also have access to the artifacts of the dead, which can be purchased for their normal Artifact value but are of no use outside the Underworld. This alteration applies only to Abyssals who continue to faithfully serve their Deathlords — renegades use the Artifact Background from the main Exalted rulebook.
ladder: None: who are you, that your Deathlord has given you no trinkets of power?
Trinkets: artifacts with a combined Artifact rating no higher than 3.
Sound Gear: artifacts with a combined Artifact rating no higher than 5. None can individually be above Artifact 3 without Storyteller permission.
Well-Equipped: artifacts with a combined Artifact rating no higher than 7. None can individually be above Artifact 4 without Storyteller permission.
Supremely Appointed: artifacts with a combined Artifact rating no higher than 10. There is no limit on individual Artifact level, other than it cannot be N/A.
Divine Regalia: artifacts with a combined Artifact rating no higher than 13. There is no limit on individual Artifact level, other than it cannot be N/A.

name: Artifact
description: Built from Magical Materials and infused with life, the bodies and Charms of the Alchemical Exalted represent the most sophisticated and powerful artifacts in Autochthonia. Yet the Chosen of the Machine Gods use far more artifacts than themselves in the defense of their nations and patron, freely drawing on the resources and unmatched technology of the Realm of Brass and Shadow. Alchemicals receive three total dots of artifacts for every dot of the Artifact Background purchased. Most of these devices are constructed from the same Magical Material as the Exalt's caste, although this is not actually required. Alchemicals may purchase a rating as high as ••••• with their Background dots during character creation even without spending bonus points, though the fourth and fifth dot still cost two dots each. Finally, Alchemicals can purchase additional Charms as artifacts with a rating equal to their minimum Essence (but cannot purchase Charms whose Trait minimums they do not meet); these Charms are kept on retainer at the Vats and do not increase the number of Charms the Alchemical may install.
